key_insight: DeepEdu-v1 combines long-context retrieval optimization with a self-improving agentic playbook to make Vietnamese curriculum tutoring faster, more local, and less hallucination-prone.
engineering_relevance: The system addresses two deployment bottlenecks for on-premise educational LLMs: long-context inference cost on consumer GPUs and weak alignment to region-specific knowledge.
method: Long-context inference amortizes token selection from per-sub-chunk to per-cluster granularity to reduce retrieval calls and TTFT.
A self-improving agentic layer curates a verified playbook from prior interactions instead of fine-tuning.
The design is aimed at preserving data sovereignty while progressively improving local knowledge reliability.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports x7.7 fewer retrieval calls, about 35% lower TTFT on long-context retrieval, nearly x2 TTFT speedup over standard vLLM, and agentic accuracy rising from 70.0% to 79.5%.
watch_item: The self-improving playbook approach may depend on the quality and coverage of verified interactions, so early errors or sparse local data could slow gains or propagate bias.
paper_title: DeepEdu-v1: Efficient and Scalable Agentic LLMs for Vietnamese Education
